Commit - Entered published corrections in lin25 in the wake of original submission and votes; corrected entry error in lin37 (Σεβασοτῦ) adjusted the presentation of words with < > additions (lins 8, 12, 29, 33); added modern regularizations in lins 3, 8, 15, 25; corrected accents in lins23–24 and added others to words with regularizations; fixed line-break in deprecated reading in lins10–11; removed ‘cf.’ before BL references; added supra linear strokes over number in lin5.

Vote - Accept-Straight-to-Finalization - Agreed with FR => <:<:ἐγκαλέσαι|reg|ἐνκαλέ̣σ̣α̣ι̣:>=PN F. Reiter (image)|ed|ἐ̣γ̣κ̣α̣λ̣έ̣σ̣ε̣ι̣ν̣:>. The future form is not covered by |reg| in this case. Published corrections to check before finalising.

Vote - ReturnToSender - The correction of the reading in Chrest.Mitt. 159, 25 from ἐ̣γ̣κ̣α̣λ̣έ̣σ̣α̣ι̣ to ἐ̣γ̣κ̣α̣λ̣ε̣ῖ̣ν̣ (as already read by Wessely in the ed.pr.!) is not convincing according to the scan available online from the Vienna collection. I would transcribe ἐνκαλέ̣σ̣α̣ι̣. But one might correct the reading to ἐγκαλέσειν in the app.

Submit - In line 25, in the clause where the vendor pledges himself not to sue the purchaser on account of the object, one very commonly uses to present and the future tense of εγκαλεω. see, e.g., SB XX 14379.26-27 (320, Karanis). The aorist, on the other hand, is not used anywhere in this context, and its reading is also doubtful in this text. I think that future tense is also palaeographically plausible.
Commit - line 25: ἐ̣γ̣κ̣α̣λ̣έ̣σ̣ε̣ι̣ν̣ instead of ἐ̣γ̣κ̣α̣λ̣έ̣σ̣α̣ι̣
Finalized - Ready.
Vote - Accept-Straight-to-Finalization - Fine.
